title: Rigveda 9.6: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.6: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.6 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 669v-670r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.6.1-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 670r
translation.original_text:
1ma̱ndrayā̍ soma̱ dhāra̍yā̱ vṛṣā̍ pavasva deva̱yuḥ | avyo̱ vāre̍ṣv asma̱yuḥ ||
2a̱bhi tyam madya̱m mada̱m inda̱v indra̱ iti̍ kṣara | a̱bhi vā̱jino̱ arva̍taḥ ||
3a̱bhi tyam pū̱rvyam mada̍ṁ suvā̱no a̍rṣa pa̱vitra̱ ā | a̱bhi vāja̍m u̱ta śrava̍ḥ ||
4anu̍ dra̱psāsa̱ inda̍va̱ āpo̱ na pra̱vatā̍saran | pu̱nā̱nā indra̍m āśata ||
5yam atya̍m iva vā̱jina̍m mṛ̱janti̱ yoṣa̍ṇo̱ daśa̍ | vane̱ krīḻa̍nta̱m atya̍vim ||
6taṁ gobhi̱r vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ rasa̱m madā̍ya de̱vavī̍taye | su̱tam bharā̍ya̱ saṁ sṛ̍ja ||
7de̱vo de̱vāya̱ dhāra̱yendrā̍ya pavate su̱taḥ | payo̱ yad a̍sya pī̱paya̍t ||
8ā̱tmā ya̱jñasya̱ raṁhyā̍ suṣvā̱ṇaḥ pa̍vate su̱taḥ | pra̱tnaṁ ni pā̍ti̱ kāvya̍m ||
9e̱vā pu̍nā̱na i̍ndra̱yur mada̍m madiṣṭha vī̱taye̍ | guhā̍ cid dadhiṣe̱ gira̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1SOMA, flow on with pleasant stream, a Bull devoted to the Gods, Our Friend, unto the woollen sieve.
2Pour hitherward, as Indra's Self, Indu, that gladdening stream of thine, And send us coursers full of strength.
3Flow to the filter hitherward, pouring that ancient gladdening juice, Streaming forth power and high renown.
4Hither the sparkling drops have flowed, like waters down a steep descent They have reached Indra purified.
5Whom, having passed the filter, ten dames cleanse, as 'twere a vigorous steed, While he disports him in the wood,–
6The steer-strong juice with milk pour forth, for feast and service of the Gods, To him who bears away the draught.
7Effused, the God flows onward with his stream to Indra, to the God, So that his milk may strengthen him.
8Soul of the sacrifice, the juice effused flows quickly on: he keeps His ancient wisdom of a Sage.
9So pouring forth, as Indra's Friend, strong drink, best Gladdener! for the feast, Thou, even in secret, storest hymns.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 670r (numbered 92r by the scribe) (OPenn image 670, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.6.1 ‹deva-yuḥ avyaḥ vāreṣu asma-yuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 670v (numbered 92v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.7.3 ‹agriyaḥ vṛṣā ava cakradat›. Verses 9.6.1-9 end on this page; 9.6.1 begins on fol. 669v (numbered 91v by the scribe).
